sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:4

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:4:1
items.html: The hairs of the Keter that surround his head from the outside, down to the forehead and to the ears: It was already explained above, page 392, the passage beginning “and although,” that the hairs are divided into two aspects, Rosh and Guf: that down to the ears, which is Bina, is reckoned as the aspect of a Rosh, since the place of the coupling was in the Nikvey Einayim, which are the Hochma of the Rosh; and therefore the lights expanded from there downward to the Ozen, Hotem and Peh, in the aspect of clothing, which is called Guf. And you already know that the difference between a Rosh and a Guf is very great. And this is what he says, that the hairs extend down to the ears — for down to there it is reckoned as the aspect of a Rosh, but from the ears downward it is already reckoned as the aspect of a Guf, as he goes on to write.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:4:2
items.html:
The hairs of the beard, which are extended from the general SAG that is called Nekudim. And you must know that these AHP, which emerged from the aspect of a Rosh into the aspect of a Guf, as above, are always called by the name of the general SAG. And the reason is as the ARI writes further on, that this whole SAG of AK with which we are occupied (8) is reckoned entirely as an aspect of AB, except for the Nekudot in it, which are its lower half, called further on by the name YESHSUT; it alone is reckoned as SAG, for it alone emerged by way of the Nikvey Einayim into the aspect of AHP of the Guf. And this YESHSUT is what is everywhere called the general SAG, and it is the Rosh of the ten Sefirot of Nekudim, as is written before us at length.
And it was explained above that the beginning of the coupling in the Nikvey Einayim, which brought out the AHP into the aspect of a Guf, was made in the Rosh of SAG itself, only in the secret of the hairs: that the hairs of the head down to the ears are discerned as the aspect of from below upward, which is a Rosh, (9) and it is therefore still discerned as an aspect of AB, since no change whatever is yet noticeable in it because of the ascent of the lower Hey to the Nikvey Einayim; but from the Nikvey Einayim downward, which are the hairs of the Dikna, they are already reckoned as the aspect of AHP that emerged from the Rosh and became an aspect of Guf. Therefore the AHP of the hairs, which are called by the name of the hairs of the Dikna, are alone reckoned as the general SAG, which is the aspect of the Nekudim. And all this will be explained further on at length, for that is its place.
And this is what he says, and afterwards he brought out the hairs of the beard, which are extended from the general SAG, called Nekudim. That is, that from the aspect of the ears downward the hairs of the beard were extended in the aspect of the general SAG, called Nekudim; but those hairs that emerge from the Nikvey Einayim — that is, from the Malchut that is in Hochma, from below upward — are still reckoned as AB and are not the branches of the general SAG, as above. So that the hairs of the head are branches extended from AB, and the hairs of the Dikna are branches extended from the general SAG. And remember this.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 6:4:3
items.html: The generality of the three Mochin in it. That is, the first three Sefirot, KHB, of Nekudim, which are made from these hairs of the beard — and not from them themselves, but only from the generality in them, which is gathered in the fourth correction of the hairs of the beard, called the Shibolet HaZakan, as is all written at length further on. And this is what he says, that from them the generality of the three Mochin in it was made.
